actions.action: Root-caused the color bug: Tailwind v4 puts every utility inside a CSS @layer, and WP core's own admin CSS is unlayered — per the cascade-layers spec, unlayered rules always beat layered ones regardless of selector specificity, so WP core's plain 'a { color: #3858e9 }' overrode '.text-white' even though a class selector normally beats an element selector. Fixed by applying Tailwind v4's trailing '!' important-modifier (border-white!, text-white!, text-white/70!, hover:text-white!) to the four color utilities in the nav, and verified '!important' actually landed in the compiled CSS before considering it fixed. Documented as knoladge/tailwind-cascade-layers-vs-wp-admin.md (noted this likely affects other admin links too, not fixed elsewhere since only the nav was reported). Built the child-theme feature: inc/child-theme.php (loaded unconditionally, mirroring inc/updater.php's pattern) with hex_generate_child_theme_slug() (collision-avoiding), hex_child_theme_style_css()/hex_child_theme_functions_php() (pure content builders, with a hex_strip_comment_terminator() defense against a theme name breaking out of the style.css header comment), hex_create_child_theme() (writes via WP_Filesystem — deliberately not unit-tested, matching the 'don't test the actual filesystem/API edge' policy already set for the main updater), and a fully separate PucFactory-based update checker for the child theme (own hex_child_github_repo/branch/activation_key options, own settings group, targets wp_get_theme($slug)'s own style.css so it works whether or not the child is the active theme). Design decision: all management (create/check/update) lives in the parent theme's admin rather than generating a duplicate mini-admin-UI into the child, since WordPress always loads the parent's functions.php even when the child is active. Added a 4th admin page/tab 'Child Theme' (inc/admin/page-child-theme.php) with a create form, a separate settings form, and Check/Update buttons; 3 new admin-post handlers; child settings fields in inc/admin/settings.php reusing hex_sanitize_github_branch() and a near-duplicate hex_sanitize_child_github_repo() (separate settings-error identifier). Added tests/ChildThemeTest.php (11 new tests) — full suite 47 tests/63 assertions passing. Fixed 2 WPCS docblock full-stop errors (hash-notation @param blocks weren't accepted by this ruleset — switched to plain single-line @param descriptions) and auto-fixed alignment warnings; 0 phpcs errors. actions.action: Root-caused: hex_is_child_theme_active()/hex_get_child_theme_slug() relied entirely on the hex_child_theme_slug OPTION, which is only ever written by hex_install_child_theme_from_repo(). The user had activated hexnity-wp-child by copying/activating it directly (not through the Fetch & Install button), so that option was never set, and the code had no way to know a child theme was active regardless of reality. Fixed by making hex_get_child_theme_slug() prefer WordPress's own live state: `is_child_theme() ? get_stylesheet() : get_option('hex_child_theme_slug','')` — the insight being that this code only executes because it's required from THIS theme's own functions.php, and WordPress always loads the parent's functions.php even when a child is active, so is_child_theme() being true here proves the active child's parent IS this theme, regardless of how that child reached disk or got activated. hex_is_child_theme_active() simplified to just is_child_theme() directly. This single change also fixes hex_check_for_child_theme_update()/hex_perform_child_theme_update(), which had the identical blind spot. Rewrote the affected tests in tests/ChildThemeTest.php (is_child_theme()-based mocking instead of get_option-based) and added 2 new ones for hex_get_child_theme_slug()'s live-vs-stored preference — full suite 53 tests/60 assertions passing, 0 phpcs errors, php -l clean. actions.action: Built a ~27-token admin-configurable design-token system. Architecture: a single PHP schema (hex_get_style_schema() in the new inc/style-settings.php, loaded unconditionally) drives everything — Settings API registration (hex_register_style_settings() in inc/admin/settings.php, one generic hex_render_style_field() renderer for all fields instead of ~27 hand-written ones), sanitization (hex_sanitize_style_length()/hex_sanitize_style_color(), both reject-and-revert-to-previous-value rather than ever storing empty/invalid — uses current_filter() to recover the option name inside the generic sanitize_option_{name} filter context), and the runtime CSS output (hex_render_style_css_vars(), hooked to wp_head, prints every current value as a --hex-{key} custom property on :root on EVERY front-end request, independent of child-theme-active state — plus hex_is_safe_style_value() as an independent output-time injection defense on top of the sanitize callbacks). Groups: typography (h1-h6 + body/lead/large/small — 10), spacing (xs/sm/md/lg/xl/2xl — 6), colors (primary/secondary/accent/muted/text/background — 6), buttons (radius + default/small/large padding-x/y — 7), radius (card — 1). Live-without-rebuild mechanism: new assets/css/src/site-theme.css defines Tailwind v4 @theme tokens as `var(--hex-{key}, {default})` — e.g. `--text-h1: var(--hex-h1-size, 2.5rem)` — so Tailwind's compiled .text-h1 utility references the runtime variable, not a baked-in value; verified this actual chain in the compiled CSS output, not just assumed it. All token names deliberately avoid colliding with Tailwind's own built-in scale (h1-h6/body/lead/large/small instead of xs/sm/lg/xl; site-primary/etc instead of blue/slate; button/card instead of sm/md/lg) so this never silently overrides existing Tailwind usage elsewhere. Also added a .btn component (+ -secondary/-accent/-outline/-sm/-lg variants), a global `a { color: var(--color-site-primary) }` base-layer default link color (loses to any more-specific existing utility via ordinary specificity), and .prose h1-h6 overrides (@tailwindcss/typography's own documented override pattern) so headings an editor types inside post content also respond to the H1-H6 settings, not just template-level titles. Gating: inc/admin/page-theme-options.php wraps every field in `<fieldset disabled>` unless hex_is_child_theme_active(), with an amber notice + link to the Child Theme page when disabled — reusing the active-detection fixed in the previous entry. Added the 5th admin tab/submenu (menu.php, partials.php) and a Dashboard quick link. Retrofitted existing front-end templates to actually use the new tokens (so the feature has real, visible effect today, not just for future pages): archive.php/404.php/search.php (h1 titles -> text-h1), comments.php (title -> text-h3, closed-notice -> text-small), template-parts/content-none.php (title -> text-h2, card -> rounded-card/p-lg), template-parts/content.php (h1/h2 titles -> text-h1/text-h2, link hover -> hover:text-site-primary, card -> rounded-card/p-md, meta/footer -> text-small), template-parts/content-page.php (title -> text-h1, page-links -> text-small), footer.php (site-info -> text-small), header.php (site-title fallback -> text-large) — chose exact-default-matching values (p-md=1.5rem=old p-6, p-lg=2rem=old p-8) where possible so today's visual output doesn't change, only becomes admin-controllable. Added tests/StyleSettingsTest.php (17 tests: schema shape, naming transforms, value resolution, CSS-var output incl. the unsafe-value-skip defense, both sanitize callbacks' revert-on-invalid behavior) — full suite 69 tests/100 assertions passing, 0 phpcs errors (after auto-fixing 23 array-alignment warnings and fixing 2 more hash-notation-docblock full-stop errors, the same WPCS friction point hit twice before), php -l clean, both CSS builds compile with all new utility classes verified present via grep. Wrote features/design-system.md — the explicit 'for future AI use' reference this was asked for, including a full class-substitution table (design-system class vs. the raw Tailwind equivalent to avoid) and a step-by-step 'adding a new token' guide. Added a MANDATORY claude.md rule pointing every future front-end styling task at that table. Bumped 1.0.5 -> 1.1.0 (minor, new feature) in all three version locations.

actions.action: Rebuilt the schema from 27 to 146 fields across 12 groups (was 5): Typography (heading levels now carry size+line-height+letter-spacing+weight+margin-bottom each, plus body/lead/large/small/meta with their own line-heights, plus body/heading font-family and link color/hover-color = 47 fields, up from 10), Spacing (unchanged, 6), Colors (expanded from 6 to a 15-color palette: primary/secondary/tertiary/accent/success/warning/danger/info/muted/emphasis/body-bg/body-text/inverse-bg/inverse-text/border), Buttons (expanded from 7 to 26: 4 full variants — default/primary/secondary/danger, each background+color+hover pair — plus text-button colors, radius, weight, 6 paddings), and 6 entirely new groups: Forms (8), Cards (6), Sections (8), Global radius (3, deliberately overrides Tailwind's own rounded-sm/md/lg site-wide), Tables (4), Alerts (8, 4 states), Badges (10, 5 variants), Icons (5). Introduced 4 new field types beyond length/color: 'number' (bare unitless line-heights), 'weight' (100-900 enum), 'shadow' (fixed keyword->real-box-shadow-CSS preset map, since raw box-shadow syntax can't safely round-trip through a text field), 'font' (safe font-family charset). Refactored sanitization: every type-specific sanitizer now shares one hex_style_revert_from_filter() helper (previously length/color had near-duplicate revert logic). Built the schema with per-family loops (heading levels, button/alert/badge variants) rather than hand-writing 146 array literals — one config change adds a whole family member. Rebuilt the admin UI per the 'not professional' complaint: replaced the flat form-table (do_settings_section/do_settings_fields) with a left-category tab nav + right detail panel (inc/admin/page-theme-options.php + new assets/js/admin.js tab-switching logic), a CSS-grid 2-column field layout instead of table rows, and native <input type=color> swatches paired with (and JS-synced to) the hex text fields instead of plain text-only color inputs. Rewrote site-theme.css to wire every new token: added @layer base rules applying full typographic treatment directly to bare h1-h6/body/a tags (so ANY heading anywhere gets the treatment, not just ones with an explicit text-h* class) and removed now-redundant/conflicting font-bold/font-semibold/tracking-tight utility classes from every retrofitted heading (they were higher-specificity than the new base rules and would have silently overridden them); added .card/.form-control+.form-label/.table-styled/.alert+4 variants/.badge+5 variants/.icon components; expanded .btn to 4 real variants (default/primary/secondary/danger) plus .btn-text/.btn-outline; extended the .prose heading overrides to include line-height/letter-spacing/weight, not just font-size. Swapped the 3 existing card usages (template-parts/content.php, content-none.php, 404.php) from ad-hoc utility composition to the real .card component. Verified in compiled CSS: .card, base h1{}, body{}, and the --radius-sm/md/lg override of rounded-sm/md/lg all resolved correctly. Needed to insert 25 individual '/* translators: %s: ... */' comments (one per sprintf(__(...)) call site in the loop-built schema, each describing the specific interpolated variable) to satisfy WPCS's WordPress.WP.I18n.MissingTranslatorsComment sniff — did this with a small Python script matching each sprintf pattern rather than by hand, then verified zero unmatched patterns. Rewrote tests/StyleSettingsTest.php's group-coverage test to check schema membership against hex_get_style_groups() dynamically (was a hardcoded 5-group list that would need updating every time a group is added) and added tests for all 4 new field types plus shadow-keyword CSS resolution — suite grew from 69 to 85 tests (100 to 419 assertions, since several new tests loop-assert or check large arrays). Rewrote features/design-system.md and the claude.md pointer rule around the full new class/component set. Bumped 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0 in all three version locations.

actions.user_requirement: User, frustrated that the previous fix (1.5.2) still showed a white background on the tab buttons, said the CSS should be `.hex-tab-btn { ...; background-color: black; }` and asked for it to be added like that.
actions.action: Previous fix (1.5.2) deliberately left .hex-tab-btn without any background-color, reasoning that appearance-none would make the background fall back to CSS-initial transparent. That reasoning was wrong: the browser's UA stylesheet sets an *explicit* background-color (ButtonFace/white) on <button>, independent of the appearance property -- appearance:none stops the native widget from being drawn, it does not clear that explicit UA background declaration. With no author rule overriding it, the button stayed white, which is what the user was still seeing ("fuck why cannt u still add dark color to that buttons. still they are white"). User then specified the exact fix wanted: add `background-color: black;` directly to .hex-tab-btn. Implemented via `bg-black!` in the component's @apply list. Because .hex-tab-btn's @layer components block is declared after admin.css's `@layer utilities` import, a plain (non-important) black background would have permanently beaten the page's hover:bg-gray-800 utility and the JS-toggled active bg-indigo-600 utility (cascade layers decide ties for equal-importance rules by declaration order, ignoring specificity) -- so both hover and active-tab highlighting would have gone dark/invisible. Fixed by making all three competing declarations !important, which moves the comparison to the importance tier instead (where the *earlier* declared layer wins, i.e. utilities beats components): changed the page's `hover:bg-gray-800` to `hover:bg-gray-800!` (inc/admin/page-theme-options.php) and admin.js's toggled class from `bg-indigo-600` to `bg-indigo-600!` (assets/js/admin.js). Verified in the compiled CSS that all three rules (.hex-tab-btn's bg-black!important, hover:bg-gray-800!:hover !important, .bg-indigo-600\!:not(:hover) !important) came out correctly. Rebuilt CSS. Bumped version 1.5.2 -> 1.5.3 in style.css, functions.php, tests/bootstrap.php. Ran vendor/bin/phpunit (103/103) and vendor/bin/phpcs --standard=phpcs.xml.dist (0 errors/warnings).
